affected_system: multichannel public-service intake, triage, dispatch, and resolution workflow
alternatives: rank verified high-consequence candidates for public-service workflow improvement portfolio
select a risk-, equity-, and lifecycle-balanced portfolio for public-service workflow improvement portfolio
pair volume, burden, equity, failure-mode, and lifecycle prioritization with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Requests, contacts, duplicates, service categories, assignments, work orders, and outcomes remain distinct.
Channel and area comparisons account for taxonomy, access, publication, and reporting differences.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: fund only already-committed work for public-service workflow improvement portfolio.

constraints.description: The 311 and public-service demand operations prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: chief service officer and 311 operations director
decision_question: Which intake, routing, self-service, field, translation, and quality improvements should be funded?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The 311 and public-service demand operations prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for public-service workflow improvement portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: volume, burden, equity, failure-mode, and lifecycle prioritization
independence_key.primary_outcome: expected avoidable request handling and resident effort

intended_claim: A versioned prioritize design for comparing declared alternatives affecting public-service workflow improvement portfolio, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: expected avoidable request handling and resident effort
distributional gap in expected avoidable request handling and resident effort
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report modeled handling savings as realized productivity or resident satisfaction.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.
reference_implementation_note: Tier-D template deep.public-service.total-demand.v1 (Citywide service-request workload baseline) supplies a bounded reference workflow for this design axis. The mapping does not establish complete city-specific inputs, external validity, deployment, adoption, or impact.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for public-service workflow improvement portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.

title: Prioritize public-service workflow improvements
transportability_risks: Service taxonomies, channels, SLAs, agency ownership, reporting, and publication rules differ.
Observed demand reflects both conditions and ability or willingness to report.
